cards.q: What is the difference between retained and immediate mode?
cards.a: Retained mode keeps widget objects you create once and update; immediate mode describes the whole interface every frame as function calls that read and write the real data directly.

cards.q: Does Dear ImGui keep any state between frames?
cards.a: Yes: window positions and sizes, open tree nodes, active widgets, scroll and text editing state, found by each widget's ID.

cards.q: Why does immediate mode avoid synchronisation bugs?
cards.a: Widgets read and write the program's real data directly every frame, so there is no second copy to keep in sync.

cards.q: Which files make up a typical Win32 + DirectX 11 ImGui set-up?
cards.a: The ImGui core .cpp and .h files plus imgui_impl_win32 and imgui_impl_dx11 from the backends folder.
cards.lessonTitle: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11

cards.q: List the calls at the start and end of every frame.
cards.a: ImGui_ImplDX11_NewFrame, ImGui_ImplWin32_NewFrame, ImGui::NewFrame at the start; ImGui::Render and ImGui_ImplDX11_RenderDrawData(ImGui::GetDrawData()) at the end.
cards.lessonTitle: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11

cards.q: In what order do you shut ImGui down?
cards.a: The renderer back end, the platform back end, then DestroyContext: the reverse of setting up.
cards.lessonTitle: Setting Up ImGui with Win32 and DirectX 11

cards.q: What is ImDrawData?
cards.a: Everything ImGui wants drawn this frame: per-window lists of vertices, indices and draw commands with textures and clipping rectangles.
cards.lessonTitle: The Frame and the Draw Data

cards.q: What is a font atlas?
cards.a: One texture holding every glyph of the loaded fonts, so text can be drawn as textured triangles.
cards.lessonTitle: The Frame and the Draw Data

cards.q: What is io.DeltaTime used for?
cards.a: The time since the last frame, used for double clicks, key repeat, cursor blinking and animations.
cards.lessonTitle: The Frame and the Draw Data

cards.q: What does Begin's return value mean, and what must you always do afterwards?
cards.a: Whether the window's contents are visible (not collapsed or clipped); End must always be called.

cards.q: How do you give a window a default size the user can change?
cards.a: SetNextWindowSize with ImGuiCond_FirstUseEver before Begin.

cards.q: When does ImGui::Button return true?
cards.a: On the frame the mouse button is released over it after being pressed over it.

cards.q: How does ImGui compute a widget's ID?
cards.a: It hashes the widget's label (or the part from ### on), seeded with the value on top of the ID stack, which windows and PushID change.

cards.q: What do ## and ### do in a label?
cards.a: ## hides everything after it from the display but keeps it in the ID; ### makes only the part from ### onward the ID.

cards.q: What goes wrong if a widget's ID changes every frame?
cards.a: It loses its remembered state every frame, so drags stop, tree nodes close and text editing resets.

cards.q: Name four debugging tools built into ImGui.
cards.a: ShowDemoWindow, the style editor, the Metrics/Debugger window (with its debug log and Item Picker), and the ID Stack tool.
cards.lessonTitle: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools

cards.q: What should you do when an IM_ASSERT fires?
cards.a: Read the comment above it in the source, which explains the rule, and fix the code that broke it.
cards.lessonTitle: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools

cards.q: Why keep imgui_demo.cpp in the project during development?
cards.a: It is the reference for every feature, and costs nothing unless ShowDemoWindow is called.
cards.lessonTitle: The Demo Window and the Debug Tools

cards.q: How does a linear slider map the mouse position to a value?
cards.a: t = (mouse x minus track start) divided by track width, clamped to 0..1; value = min + t times (max minus min).

cards.q: What does ImGuiSliderFlags_Logarithmic change?
cards.a: The position maps to the logarithm of the value, giving equal room to each order of magnitude.

cards.q: Name three IsItem functions and what they tell you.
cards.a: IsItemHovered (mouse over it), IsItemActive (being used now), IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit (the edit just finished and changed the value).

cards.q: How do you edit a std::string with InputText?
cards.a: Include misc/cpp/imgui_stdlib and pass a pointer to the string; it resizes as you type.

cards.q: Name four flags that restrict or change text input.
cards.a: CharsDecimal, CharsHexadecimal, CharsUppercase, CharsNoBlank, EnterReturnsTrue, ReadOnly, Password.

cards.q: Describe the pattern for validated editing.
cards.a: Edit a copy, show the validation message as you type, and copy the value back only when the edit finishes and the value is valid.

cards.q: What does Selectable do and where is it used?
cards.a: It draws a full-width clickable row that can show as selected; it is used in combos, list boxes, tables and trees.

cards.q: When would you use BeginCombo instead of the one-line Combo?
cards.a: When the items are not a simple string array: vectors of objects, items with extra drawing, or filtered lists.

cards.q: What makes a good filter for a long list?
cards.a: Case-insensitive matching where every word of the filter appears somewhere in the item, in any order.

cards.q: What are ImGui's two forms of colour, and where is each used?
cards.a: ImVec4, four floats 0..1, used by widgets and styles; ImU32, four packed bytes, used by draw lists.

cards.q: Why does IM_COL32 put red in the lowest byte?
cards.a: So that in memory on a little-endian machine the bytes are R, G, B, A, the vertex colour format the GPU reads.

cards.q: How do you give each of many items a distinct colour?
cards.a: Spread hues by the golden ratio (hue = i times 0.618 modulo 1) at fixed saturation and value, then convert HSV to RGB.

cards.q: What is the rule for sharing input between ImGui and a game?
cards.a: Give ImGui the input first; the game only handles the mouse when WantCaptureMouse is false and the keyboard when WantCaptureKeyboard is false.

cards.q: Name four input queries ImGui offers your code.
cards.a: IsKeyPressed, IsKeyDown, IsMouseClicked, IsMouseDragging, IsMouseDoubleClicked, GetMousePos, io.MouseDelta.

cards.q: Why prefer ImGui::Shortcut over checking keys yourself in a tool?
cards.a: It respects focus and routing, so shortcuts do not fire while typing elsewhere, and handles modifiers consistently.

cards.q: How does ImGui decide where a widget goes?
cards.a: At the window's layout cursor, which moves to the next line after each widget unless SameLine or other layout calls change it.

cards.q: Why measure sizes from the font and the available region?
cards.a: So the layout adapts to other font sizes, display scaling and window sizes.

cards.q: What does a group do?
cards.a: It makes several widgets act as one item for layout and item queries, so the whole group can be placed on a line or hovered.

cards.q: What does a negative child size mean?
cards.a: Fill the available space minus that amount, leaving room for widgets after the child.

cards.q: How does ImGuiListClipper make a huge list cheap?
cards.a: It computes which equal-height items are visible from the scroll position and draws only those, while reserving space for the rest.

cards.q: How do you make a log follow new lines without fighting the user?
cards.a: Before adding lines, check whether the scroll is at the bottom; only then scroll to the new bottom.

cards.q: What does TableSetupScrollFreeze(0, 1) do?
cards.a: Keeps the first row, normally the headers, visible while the table scrolls.

cards.q: Describe how to sort a table's data.
cards.a: After setting up the columns, get TableGetSortSpecs; if SpecsDirty, sort the data comparing column by column in spec order with each direction, then clear SpecsDirty.

cards.q: Why compare by a column's user ID rather than its index?
cards.a: Columns can be reordered or hidden, so a stable ID keeps each column's meaning.

cards.q: What are the Leaf and NoTreePushOnOpen flags for?
cards.a: Leaf draws a node without an arrow for items with no children; NoTreePushOnOpen means TreePop must not be called for it.

cards.q: What is the anchor in multi-selection?
cards.a: The last item clicked without Shift; Shift+click selects from it to the clicked item in display order.

cards.q: How do you open a tree node from code to reveal a selected object?
cards.a: Call SetNextItemOpen(true) before drawing each of its ancestors.

cards.q: Which pairs follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule in this lesson?
cards.a: BeginTabBar/EndTabBar, BeginTabItem/EndTabItem, and BeginTooltip-style item tooltips (BeginItemTooltip/EndTooltip).

cards.q: How do you select a tab from code?
cards.a: Pass ImGuiTabItemFlags_SetSelected to its BeginTabItem on that frame.

cards.q: Why wrap tooltip text?
cards.a: Unwrapped long text makes the tooltip wider than the screen; pushing a wrap position keeps it readable.

cards.q: Which menu functions follow the "End only if Begin returned true" rule?
cards.a: BeginMainMenuBar/EndMainMenuBar, BeginMenuBar/EndMenuBar and BeginMenu/EndMenu.

cards.q: How do you make a menu's shortcut actually work?
cards.a: Check the key chord yourself, for example with ImGui::Shortcut, once per frame outside the menu code.

cards.q: Why build menus from a command table?
cards.a: One list drives the menu, the shortcuts and a command palette, keeps availability checks in one place, and lets you detect shortcut clashes.

cards.q: Describe ImGui's popup model.
cards.a: A popup has an ID; OpenPopup marks it open once, and BeginPopup, called every frame, returns true and draws it while it is open; it closes on outside clicks, Escape, selectables or CloseCurrentPopup.

cards.q: What do BeginPopupContextItem and BeginPopupContextWindow do?
cards.a: They open and begin a popup when the item just drawn, or empty space in the window, is right-clicked.

cards.q: How do you centre a modal each time it appears?
cards.a: SetNextWindowPos at the main viewport's centre, with pivot (0.5, 0.5) and ImGuiCond_Appearing.

cards.q: What does SetDragDropPayload do with the data you pass?
cards.a: It copies it, so the payload is safe even if the source changes, as long as it holds values such as ids rather than pointers.

cards.q: When does AcceptDragDropPayload return non-null?
cards.a: On the frame the mouse button is released over the target with a payload of the accepted type.

cards.q: What check must re-parenting by drag and drop make?
cards.a: That the new parent is not the dragged node itself or any of its descendants.

cards.q: What two config flags turn on docking and multiple viewports?
cards.a: ImGuiConfigFlags_DockingEnable and ImGuiConfigFlags_ViewportsEnable.

cards.q: What extra calls does the loop need with multiple viewports?
cards.a: ImGui::UpdatePlatformWindows and ImGui::RenderPlatformWindowsDefault after rendering the main window.

cards.q: How do you give first-time users a sensible layout?
cards.a: Build it with the DockBuilder API when the dockspace has no saved layout, and offer it again from a reset menu item.

cards.q: How do you change a style value for just one widget?
cards.a: PushStyleColor or PushStyleVar before it and the matching Pop after it.

cards.q: How should a tool handle a 200% display scale?
cards.a: Multiply the style sizes with ScaleAllSizes and load fonts at the scaled pixel size.

cards.q: Why are ImGui labels UTF-8, and what does that mean for icons?
cards.a: ImGui reads all strings as UTF-8; icon code points in the private use area must be written as their multi-byte UTF-8 sequences.

cards.q: Describe the format of imgui.ini.
cards.a: Sections headed [Type][Name], each followed by Key=Value lines, for windows, tables, docking and any custom handlers.

cards.q: What must be true of the string assigned to io.IniFilename?
cards.a: It must stay valid for as long as ImGui uses it, because ImGui stores only the pointer.

cards.q: When must custom settings handlers be added?
cards.a: Before the first NewFrame, because that is when the ini file is read.

cards.q: How does a ring buffer feed a scrolling graph?
cards.a: New samples overwrite the oldest in a fixed array; the graph starts drawing from the oldest sample's index, given as the offset.

cards.q: Name two ways to smooth a noisy value.
cards.a: A moving average over the last N samples, and exponential smoothing: smoothed += (value - smoothed) * k.

cards.q: How do you map a value to a y position in a custom graph?
cards.a: y = top + height * (1 - (value - min) / (max - min)), so larger values are higher on screen.

cards.q: Describe ImGuiTextFilter's syntax.
cards.a: Comma-separated terms checked in order, ignoring case; the first term found in the line decides (a plain term shows it, a term starting with - hides it); if none is found, the line passes only when there are no inclusions.

cards.q: How do you make logging thread-safe?
cards.a: Protect the entries with a mutex, or have threads push into a queue the UI thread drains each frame.

cards.q: How do you keep filtering cheap?
cards.a: Recompute the list of matching indexes only when the filter changes, and check only new entries as they arrive.

cards.q: How does a field table let one function inspect any type?
cards.a: Each entry gives a field's name, kind and offset, so the function can find the field inside any object and pick the right widget.

cards.q: How should an inspector show a field for several selected objects?
cards.a: Normally if all values are equal, as mixed if they differ, and an edit writes the new value to every selected object.

cards.q: What must be true of a type for offsetof to be reliable?
cards.a: It must be standard-layout: a plain struct without virtual functions or mixed access specifiers.

cards.q: Describe the do, undo and redo operations on two stacks.
cards.a: Do: apply, push on undo, clear redo. Undo: pop undo, revert, push on redo. Redo: pop redo, apply, push on undo.

cards.q: Why should changes store ids rather than pointers?
cards.a: Objects can be deleted and recreated by undo at a different address; ids stay valid.

cards.q: How does a group of changes undo correctly?
cards.a: It reverts its changes in the reverse order they were applied.

cards.q: Why does zooming need to adjust the pan?
cards.a: To keep the point under the mouse in place; otherwise the view jumps towards the origin with every zoom step.

cards.q: Why use an InvisibleButton over the canvas?
cards.a: It gives hover, active and click state for the whole area and stops mouse drags from moving the window.

cards.q: Why should flood fill not be recursive?
cards.a: A large region needs one call per tile, which can overflow the call stack; an explicit stack or queue cannot.

cards.q: How do begin and end events become a tree?
cards.a: Walk them in order with a stack: a begin pushes a child of the current top; an end pops the top and records its duration.

cards.q: What is the difference between total and self time?
cards.a: Total time is the whole span of a zone; self time is the total minus the time spent in its child zones.

cards.q: Why should zone names be string literals?
cards.a: Their pointers stay valid forever, so recording a zone costs no allocation or copying.

cards.q: Name the three choices for ImGui in a shipped game.
cards.a: Compile it out, keep it hidden behind a key or flag, or keep some tools as real player-facing features.
cards.lessonTitle: ImGui in a Game You Ship

cards.q: Where does ImGui's cost usually come from?
cards.a: From the CPU time of building debug windows each frame, especially ones that loop over many objects; memory goes to the font atlas.
cards.lessonTitle: ImGui in a Game You Ship

cards.q: What must you check about input when tools are hidden?
cards.a: That nothing can take keyboard or mouse focus while hidden, so the game always receives its input.
cards.lessonTitle: ImGui in a Game You Ship
